critique:
GO covers only the source and metadata stage: bounded acquisition of the two selected CSVs, source-integrity checks, and metadata-field mapping. It authorizes no fitting, count interpretation, final split, or held-out scoring. The exact plan calls for a separate code review before the reader runs.
This is an independent review of the expanded card and its hash-pinned plan. It does not reuse the earlier peer review, whose GO was limited to row-free source and measurement-contract review.
The plan resolves the earlier source-stage holds: it limits methods context to already inspected Dryad usage notes without another paper request; maps all prey, predator, and parasite combinations against four explicit prey-present arms; requires PARA and conditional DIDI coverage per candidate repID; and keeps count and Colonies opaque without outcome-based row deletion.
The card's cheap_test field does not name the plan's SERRA coverage, missingness, and join-report requirements. Because the card hash-pins this plan and calls for a full per-unit coverage map, I read the plan's more specific output contract as governing. The implementation and receipt must include that complete SERRA map and preserve unmatched records.
No source-stage blocker remains if the stage follows the plan's pre-GET identity, license, size, checksum, byte-cap, and request-cap checks. Unresolved microcosm independence, cross-file unit joins, exposure units, and sampling/removal facts remain future fit-readiness risks and require HOLD for any fit until resolved or explicitly bounded in a separately reviewed design.
